record.paper_title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems
record.original_question: For the general copolymer model, the free energy near criticality is known to satisfy F(λ, h_c(λ)+δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ^2 for every δ > 0 under the stated disorder assumptions. Can this smoothing bound be improved by replacing the exponent 2 with a larger exponent?

evidence.quote: for every λ > 0 there exists c(λ) < ∞ such that F(λ,hc(λ) +δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ2 for every δ > 0.
A natural open question however is: ? Can one improve (20), in the sense of replacing the exponent 2 with a larger value?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\omega = (\omega_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. real random variables under a probability measure $\mathbb{P}$, satisfying $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1] = 0$, $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1^2] = 1$, and $M(t) := \mathbb{E}[\exp(t\omega_1)] < \infty$ for all $t$ in a neighborhood of $0$. Let $S = (S_n)_{n \geq 0}$ be a simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ starting at $0$, with law $\mathbf{P}$, and define $\Delta_n = \mathrm{sign}(S_n) \in \{-1, 0, +1\}$ (with the convention that $\mathrm{sign}(0)$ is determined by an arbitrary fixed rule, e.g., $\mathrm{sign}(0) = +1$).

For parameters $\lambda \geq 0$ and $h \in \mathbb{R}$, and an integer $N \geq 1$, define the copolymer Hamiltonian
$$H_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h)(S) = \lambda \sum_{n=1}^{N} (\omega_n + h)\, \Delta_n,$$
the partition function $Z_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h) = \mathbf{E}\!\left[\exp\!\left(H_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h)(S)\right)\right]$, and the quenched free energy
$$\textsf{F}(\lambda,h) = \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N}\, \mathbb{E}\!\left[\log Z_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h)\right] - \lambda h,$$
which exists, is non-negative, and is non-increasing in $h$. The quenched critical point is
$$h_c(\lambda) = \inf\{h \in \mathbb{R} : \textsf{F}(\lambda,h) = 0\}.$$
The simple random walk return time satisfies $\mathbf{P}(\tau_1 = 2n) \sim C n^{-3/2}$ as $n \to \infty$, so the underlying renewal exponent is $\alpha = 1/2$.

Known smoothing bound. For every $\lambda > 0$ there exists $c(\lambda) < \infty$ such that
$$0 \leq \textsf{F}(\lambda, h_c(\lambda) + \delta) \leq (1+\alpha)\, c(\lambda)\, \delta^{2} \qquad \text{for every } \delta > 0.$$

Question. Can the exponent $2$ in this upper bound be improved? That is, do there exist $\lambda_0 > 0$, $\gamma > 2$, $\delta_0 > 0$, and a finite constant $C(\lambda_0)$ such that
$$\textsf{F}(\lambda_0, h_c(\lambda_0) + \delta) \leq C(\lambda_0)\, \delta^{\gamma} \qquad \text{for all } 0 < \delta < \delta_0,$$
or, alternatively, prove that no such improvement is possible (e.g., establish a matching lower bound $\textsf{F}(\lambda, h_c(\lambda) + \delta) \geq c'(\lambda)\, \delta^{2}$ for small $\delta > 0$)?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has refined the smoothing inequality of Giacomin–Toninelli (sharper constants, weaker disorder assumptions, extension to correlated disorder), but the quadratic exponent $\gamma = 2$ has not been improved. No source found that establishes a smoothing exponent strictly greater than $2$ at criticality for the copolymer model, so the question of whether $\delta^2$ can be replaced by $\delta^{\gamma}$ with $\gamma > 2$ appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A general smoothing inequality for disordered polymers
status_evidence.snippet: Sharpens the smoothing inequality of Giacomin and Toninelli, valid for any disorder with locally finite exponential moments, with an asymptotically sharp constant in weak disorder; the exponent remains 2.
status_evidence.claim: Refinements after 2010 still give a quadratic bound F ≤ C δ^2 with no improvement of the exponent.

status_evidence.title: On the critical curves of the pinning and copolymer models
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the smoothing inequality 0 ≤ F(β, h_c+δ) ≤ (1+α) 2Υ∞ δ^2 for copolymer/pinning; the quadratic form is preserved.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to use the δ^2 bound for the copolymer free energy near criticality.
